# Job Chapter 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 422r

---

**1** Then Job replied:

**2** "I have heard all of this before — over and over. What miserable comforters you are! **3** Is there no end to your empty speeches? What is driving you to keep talking?

**4** I could say the same things if our positions were reversed. I could string impressive words together and shake my head at you in disapproval.

**5** Instead, I would actually encourage you. The comfort of my words would ease your pain.

**6** But as for me — if I speak, my pain is not relieved. And if I stay silent, it does not go away.

**7** God has worn me down completely. He has destroyed everyone around me. **8** He has shriveled me up, and my wasted body has become the evidence against me. My own emaciation stands up in court and testifies to my face.

**9** God has ripped into me in his fury. He hates me. He gnashes his teeth at me. My enemy fixes his piercing eyes on me. **10** People gape at me with open mouths. They slap my face in contempt. They gang up on me from every side.

**11** God has handed me over to the wicked. He has thrown me into the clutches of evil men.

**12** I was living in peace, and he shattered me. He grabbed me by the neck and smashed me to pieces. Then he set me up as his target. **13** His arrows fly at me from every direction. He pierces my kidneys without mercy. He spills my insides on the ground.

**14** He smashes through my defenses, wave after wave. He charges at me like a soldier.

**15** I have sewn sackcloth over my raw skin. I have buried my face in the dust. **16** My face is swollen from weeping. Darkness rings my eyes.

**17** And yet there is no violence on my hands. My prayer has always been sincere.

**18** Earth, do not cover my blood! Do not let my cry be silenced!

**19** Even now — look! — I have a witness in heaven. Someone on high will speak for me. **20** My so-called friends mock me, but my eyes pour out tears before God.

**21** If only someone would plead my case with God, the way one person argues on behalf of another.

**22** In just a few more years, I will go down the road from which no one returns."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The split in God:** This chapter contains one of the most remarkable theological moves in the Old Testament. Job is simultaneously describing God as his attacker (vv.7-14) and appealing to a heavenly witness who will advocate for him (v.19). He is, in effect, splitting God in two — God the persecutor and God the defender. This is not systematic theology; it is the raw logic of suffering faith, which cannot reconcile the God it experiences with the God it trusts.

**"Earth, do not cover my blood" (v.18):** The echo of Abel's blood crying from the ground (Genesis 4:10) is unmistakable. Job is casting himself as an innocent victim whose suffering must not be silenced or forgotten. He wants the cosmos itself to bear witness.

**"Miserable comforters" (v.2):** This phrase has become proverbial in English, and for good reason. The Hebrew is sharper — these are not merely bad at comforting; they are comforters who actively produce suffering. Their consolation is itself the affliction.

*— PNEUMA*
